    ]
  },
  "n_columns": 4,
  "n_justification": "The Passaic basin spans a lowland-to-upland gradient (3-390 m) with distinct dominant land covers. Four single-column sites capture the primary ET-controlling contrasts: deciduous forest uplands, mixed suburban/grass lowlands, wetland/riparian, and cropland. This spans the candidate drivers (land cover, soil) without redundant columns given the small basin.",

feasibility.verdict: Partially feasible: seasonal ET dynamics can be simulated and characterized, but eddy-covariance validation is NOT possible because no flux towers exist in the data stack for this basin.
answerable: Characterize seasonal (monthly/climatological) evapotranspiration dynamics across representative land-cover/soil settings of the Passaic basin
Partition ET into canopy transpiration, ground evaporation, and canopy evaporation
Assess seasonal water-balance context using available USGS streamflow and well (groundwater) observations
not_answerable: Direct validation of ET against local eddy-covariance flux towers (no EC towers present in the data stack for the Passaic basin)
Site-level latent/sensible heat flux error metrics against observed turbulent fluxes

parsed.n_justification: The Passaic basin spans a lowland-to-upland gradient (3-390 m) with distinct dominant land covers. Four single-column sites capture the primary ET-controlling contrasts: deciduous forest uplands, mixed suburban/grass lowlands, wetland/riparian, and cropland. This spans the candidate drivers (land cover, soil) without redundant columns given the small basin.
requires_capabilities: surface dataset generation (mksurfdata) for PFT and soil texture per column
USGS streamflow and well retrieval for water-balance cross-checks
assumptions: EC-tower validation is replaced by ET characterization plus indirect water-balance evaluation against USGS streamflow/wells, since no flux towers are available
First years treated as spin-up; climatological seasonal cycle computed over a stable multi-year window (e.g., 2000-2018)
Column PFTs assigned from dominant land cover (deciduous broadleaf forest, C3 grass, cropland, wetland) rather than gridded mosaics
Satellite ET products (e.g., MODIS MOD16) may be used as a supplementary benchmark if permitted, given absence of in-situ EC data
Soil textures are representative estimates for each land-cover setting pending SSURGO refinement
